named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Journal article examining, under French law, when a robot granted "electronic person" status is born or dies. Applies the analysis to a real smart android and a fictional biodroid, proposing that birth equals first activation and that non-autonomous modification of its thought system creates a new entity.
key_provisions_or_claims: Birth of a smart android corresponds to its first activation, by analogy with humans.
Modification of the AI/thought system not resulting from autonomous development creates a new entity and ends the prior one.
Electronic person status is lost by the prior version and must be reassessed for the new one.
Software updates differ from hardware repairs, which do not change identity.
Introduces the biodroid, an artificial bio-cybernetic hybrid, as a legal personhood case.
annotation.title_clean: Legal Personhood and Robotics: Birth of the Smart Android and of the Biodroid
annotation.title_en: Legal Personhood and Robotics: Birth of the Smart Android and of the Biodroid
